definitions.explanation: The head of government in a parliamentary system.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{首相|しゅしょう}が{選|えら}ばれた。
examples.english: A new prime minister was elected.

examples.japanese: {首相|しゅしょう}が{記者|きしゃ}{会見|かいけん}を{開|ひら}いた。
examples.english: The prime minister held a press conference.

examples.japanese: {首相|しゅしょう}は{経済|けいざい}{政策|せいさく}について{国民|こくみん}に{説明|せつめい}した。{野党|やとう}からは{批判|ひはん}の{声|こえ}も{上|あ}がっているが、{支持|しじ}する{意見|いけん}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: The prime minister explained the economic policy to the people. There are also critical voices from the opposition, but there are many supportive opinions as well.

notes:
{首相|しゅしょう} refers to the prime minister - the head of government in parliamentary systems.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {首相|しゅしょう}{官邸|かんてい} (prime minister's official residence)
- {首相|しゅしょう}{補佐官|ほさかん} (prime minister's aide)
- {元|もと}{首相|しゅしょう} (former prime minister)
- {現|げん}{首相|しゅしょう} (current prime minister)
- {首相|しゅしょう}{会談|かいだん} (summit meeting between prime ministers)

NOTE ON TERMINOLOGY:
- {首相|しゅしょう}: prime minister (general term, used for Japan and other countries)
- {総理|そうり} / {総理|そうり}{大臣|だいじん}: prime minister (Japan's official title)

In casual speech, Japanese people often say {総理|そうり} instead of {首相|しゅしょう} when referring to Japan's prime minister.
